headline: Gut microbiome and host transcriptomic data consolidated into reusable public databases
label: Gut Microbiome Data Resources
summary: GutBiomeDB spans 168 464 samples and gutDBase integrates 175 datasets across 15 gut-related diseases, consolidating gut data for reuse.
synthesis: The dominant thread is the consolidation of gut-related data into public, reusable databases. GutBiomeDB integrates human gut microbiome data from 168 464 samples, while gutDBase combines transcriptomic and microbial data from 175 bulk and single-cell datasets spanning 15 gut-related diseases, with interactive access. What is new in gutDBase is the joint organization of host transcriptomic and microbial layers across multiple disease contexts within one resource, rather than a shared analytical method. The other two items do not address the gut. GPBench harmonizes 16-species genomic prediction datasets and evaluates 21 GP models, and PmiREN3.0 provides a multi-omics encyclopedia for plant microRNA research.
